methodology.coverage: Every EN/TR/DE/NL primary form and every stored alternative in lexicon.json, european.json and expanded-lexicon.json receives systematic text, Unicode/script, sense-presence, POS-metadata and register validation. Explicitly recorded corrections and suspect frequency candidates were individually reviewed by the coding assistant.
methodology.semanticLimit: This is model-assisted editorial review, not native-speaker certification or a claim that all dictionary translations have been semantically verified. Automated validation can identify malformed records but cannot establish translation correctness. Correct rare or specialist meanings are not replaced solely because of low frequency.
methodology.selection: For each proposed modernization the exact English meaning and POS were inspected. Native subtitle frequency was used only as supporting evidence. Suspect high-frequency alternatives were rejected when they changed meaning, register or grammatical role.
methodology.reviewer: coding assistant; model-assisted individual sense review

globalPolicies.policy: Exclude exact alphabet-letter-name meanings before frequency selection. Do not exclude all one-character forms: English I/a and Turkish o have valid pronoun/article meanings.
Highest frequency does not prove equivalence. A replacement must preserve the selected dictionary sense and grammatical role.
Source parent glosses can belong to another meaning. Exact translation heading and translation table determine meaning; parent POS/topic nesting can be corrupted.
Attested alternatives retain their complete form metadata. Editorial corrections are explicitly identified and must not be described as verbatim dictionary records.
Do not promote alternatives marked obsolete/archaic/dialectal from source qualifiers into general learner decks merely because another metric ranks them highly.
Do not replace a valid precise technical word with a broader common word simply to increase frequency.
